newsitem.title: GREECE: FOUR DEAD, TWO MISSING AFTER STORMS LASH GREECE.
newsitem.headline: FOUR DEAD, TWO MISSING AFTER STORMS LASH GREECE.

text.p: Four people were dead and two missing after heavy storms battered Greece over the weekend, cutting power and roads and causing extensive damage.
Towns and villages dug out from heeps of muddy rubble and assessed damages in the millions of dollars. Thousands of homes, shops and buildings suffered heavy water damage.

Worse hit was Corinth, 85 kms (50 miles) west of Athens, where a river jumped its banks and inundated the town. Flood waters churned through Corinth, sweeping away scores of cars on Sunday. Water reached window sills.
Bulldozers cleared away mounts of debris and mud on Monday in Corinth after the flood water had receded. Electricity and telephones were cut in many areas around Greece and were still out on Monday.
There were traffic snarls around Athens. Motorists inched to work with traffic lights knocked out by the storms. Some main roads around Greece were still cut by flooding.
Heavy damages were reported throughout the Peloponnese peninsula, western areas near Larissa and suburbs of Athens.
Both Athens' fashionable northern suburb of Kifissia and the seaside suburb of Glyfada were awash on Sunday. Water lapped the windows of boutiques and shops.
By Monday most of the water had receded and crews were out trying to clean up the mess, aggravated by a five-day rubbish collectors' strike.
Streams of garbage swept through the streets of Kifissia, and other areas of Athens, piling up along sidewalks and shop windows.
Mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos said the capital had suffered considerable damage but its main problem was the strike.
He told a radio interviewer there were now 8,000 tonnes of rubbish in Athens and the rain had thwarted plans to stray the festering heeps with disinfectant. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
